project_specification.project_name: nullius — derivatives inputs: funding, perp–spot basis, taker flow and open interest as point-in-time features (the M2 inputs pivot)
project_specification.addition_summary: Two pre-registered M2 tests failed (docs/preregistration/*RESULT.md): - Weekly cost-aware selection: almost no node survived costs. - 2-weekly cadence: 2 of 10 campaigns found a cost-surviving node. Both were positive out of sample, but the rule needs breadth. PRD §2.3's next pivot is inputs. Signals today see only daily spot close/volume. Binance's free public archive (data.binance.vision, USD-M futures) holds full history for: - funding rates - futures klines, giving perp–spot basis and taker-buy volume - daily open-interest and long/short "metrics" This spec brings them into the lake, the sealed snapshot and the agent's window as point-in-time daily features through the existing contract.MarketWindow.feature(name, version) accessor. The contract is unchanged, so the gVisor runtime root needs no re-provisioning. Trading stays spot-only; these are signals, not instruments, so the cost model is unchanged.

existing_context.stack: Python 3.12 / uv-workspace / Parquet lake / SQLite / pytest.
existing_context.test_baseline: main at 577ec32: gate 1663 passed; orchestrator 601 passed 5 skipped.
existing_context.conventions: Follow CLAUDE.md. Existing pieces, per a code map on 2026-10-12: - ingest bars_backfill.py: - archive helpers: ARCHIVE_BASE_URL/LISTING_URL ~:337, _request_archive ~:610, _list_archive_keys ~:652, _verify_checksum ~:775, the zip cache ~:801-897, listing and rank caches, --workers, --restart - hard-coded to spot 1d: ARCHIVE_KLINES_PREFIX ~:345, _ARCHIVE_KEY_RE ~:606, _month_zip_url ~:796, _INTERVAL ~:350 - bars partitions: staging/bars/symbol=S/date=D/part-0.parquet, timestamp us UTC, values as venue strings - snapshot seal.py ~:163/:205 refuses any staging path outside bars/. The mount (partitions/select) is stream-generic. - evaluator _window.py ~:130: SLICED_STREAMS = (bars, trades, bookfeat, borrow). - orchestrator _evaluate.py: the materializer ~:512-547 builds only the bars:1d frame. _symbol_panel ~:423 is hard-coded to BARS_STREAM, the panel cache is _PANELS, and the max_history_days cap applies. - contract window.py: feature(name, version) reads frame feature:<name>:<version> and takes trailing rows across the whole frame. It does not truncate at t, so the host must cut point-in-time first. - signal-agent _authoring.py: _available_streams ~:648, _stream_columns ~:615, _accessors_detail ~:379. - The point-in-time cutoff: decision time is the end of day D, and the daily bar for D is included. Forward returns are close[i+h]/close[i].

category.name: Ingest
category.feature: System backfills USD-M futures funding rates, futures daily klines and daily open-interest metrics from the free archive into point-in-time daily lake streams, so that `./run.sh lake-derivs-backfill --lake L --first A --last B --symbols-from L/universe.json` returns funding, basis-input and metrics partitions for the spot universe. - bars_backfill's archive helpers are parametrised by archive prefix, key pattern and interval, with no behaviour change for spot bars; the existing bars tests still pass. derivs_backfill.py reuses them: the S3 listing, checksum verification, zip cache, rank-free symbol list from universe.json, --workers, resumable months and days, and --restart. - Symbol mapping: a spot symbol S maps to the UM perpetual S, or to "1000"+S when only the scaled contract exists (e.g. PEPEUSDT to 1000PEPEUSDT). The scale factor is recorded. A symbol with no perpetual has no rows. The mapping is written to staging-meta/um-symbol-map.json. - Stream funding/, from data/futures/um/monthly/fundingRate: one row per symbol per day D with - funding_rate_sum: the sum of the settlements with calcTime in (D 00:00, D+1 00:00]; a settlement at D+1 00:00 belongs to D - funding_rate_last: the last settlement in that window - n_settlements Rows exist only on days with at least one settlement. - Stream futbars/, from data/futures/um/monthly/klines/S/1d: one row per day with fut_close, fut_volume, taker_buy_volume and quote_volume, rescaled for 1000-contracts so fut_close is on the spot price scale. - Stream metrics/, from data/futures/um/daily/metrics: one row per day built from the last 5-minute snapshot strictly before D+1 00:00, with sum_open_interest, sum_open_interest_value, count_toptrader_long_short_ratio, sum_toptrader_long_short_ratio, count_long_short_ratio and sum_taker_long_short_vol_ratio. A trailing row stamped D+1 00:00 is dropped. It is opt-in with --streams metrics, because it is about 30x more files than the other two. - Timestamps are normalised from ms or µs (by magnitude, as klines.py does) to timestamp("us","UTC"). Values are written as strings, matching the bars convention. Nothing is ever forward-filled past a symbol's last archive day. - Layout: staging/<stream>/symbol=S/date=D/part-0.parquet, with S the spot symbol. - run.sh gains a lake-derivs-backfill verb, like lake-backfill. - test_derivs_backfill.py, with pinned small zips and their CHECKSUM files in tests/fixtures/binance_archive_um/ (provenance in the test module's docstring), covers: - the funding day-boundary rule, including the D+1 00:00 settlement - the 1000-scale mapping and price rescale - the metrics last-snapshot rule and the dropped trailing row - ms and µs inputs - resume without refetch - a checksum mismatch that skips the month, reports it and exits 1 - spot bars backfill unchanged No network, and it passes under pytest-xdist.

category.name: Snapshot and Window
category.feature: System seals the derivative streams beside bars, so that `./run.sh lake-seal` returns a snapshot whose mount lists funding, futbars and metrics partitions. - seal.py's allow-list admits bars, funding, futbars and metrics, in one documented constant. Every other stray path is still refused. The manifest and hash cover the new files. - test_seal_derivs_streams.py covers: - a staging tree with all four streams seals, and mount.partitions and select answer for each - an unknown stream is still refused It passes under pytest-xdist.

System serves the derivative streams in every node's window as point-in-time feature frames, so that a signal returns funding, basis, taker-flow and open-interest features through ctx.feature(name, version). - evaluator._window.SLICED_STREAMS adds funding, futbars and metrics. The tradable roster stays bars-derived. - The materializer adds, for the per-date PIT universe, frames drawn from per-(stream, symbol) panels (the _symbol_panel cache, extended with a stream key). The rows are partition date ≤ D (the end-of-D cutoff, identical to bars) and within max_history_days: - feature:funding_1d:v1 with symbol, open_time (D 00:00 UTC), funding_rate_sum, funding_rate_last and n_settlements - feature:basis_1d:v1 with symbol, open_time and basis = fut_close/spot_close − 1, computed host-side as a string. It is only present when both bars exist for D. - feature:taker_flow_1d:v1 with symbol, open_time and taker_buy_ratio = taker_buy_volume/fut_volume - feature:metrics_1d:v1 with the metrics columns, only when the metrics stream is sealed Each frame is sorted by (symbol, open_time). A symbol absent from a stream has no rows: it is never zero-filled. - The windows served are point-in-time. No row dated after D ever reaches the sandbox. A test asserts this for every frame over a grid of dates. - Bars windows are unchanged, row for row; the existing panel equivalence tests still pass. - test_window_derivs_features.py, over a tmp sealed snapshot with all streams, covers: - each frame's columns, the per-date PIT cut and the history cap - basis is computed only where both closes exist - a symbol with no perpetual is absent - frames are absent when their stream is not sealed - a stub signal reading ctx.feature("funding_1d","v1") gets the rows It passes under pytest-xdist.

category.name: Agent Contract
category.feature: System declares the served derivative features to the authoring agent, so that the rendered prompt displays each feature's name, version, columns, meaning and point-in-time rule. - accessors_detail and the available-streams statement name exactly the feature frames the materializer serves for the configured snapshot (funding_1d, basis_1d, taker_flow_1d, and metrics_1d when sealed). Raw stream names that are not served as frames are not advertised as readable. - Each feature lists: - its columns, as strings that must be cast to Float64 - one line of meaning, e.g. "funding_rate_sum: the day's summed 8-hourly perpetual funding; positive means longs pay shorts" or "basis: perpetual close over spot close minus 1" - that ctx.feature(name, version, lookback=N) takes the trailing N rows across the whole frame, not per symbol, so a signal must filter and group by symbol - A second example signal uses funding_1d with a per-symbol group-by. It is tested to run over a sealed fixture and to give non-constant scores. - test_prompt_derivs_features.py covers: - the declaration lists exactly the served frames for a snapshot with and without metrics - the example runs and normalises - every other rendered section is unchanged It passes under pytest-xdist. The signal-agent member suite passes.
